---
title: "How do I predict a new observation from a fitted regression?"
---

## Question

How do I predict a new observation from a fitted regression?

## Decide which method fits

Fit the model to paired predictor and response values; specify a new predictor within the observed range; request a prediction interval rather than silently treating the predicted mean as certain.

## Worked example: cars

```{r}
#| eval: false
d <- ru_data("cars")
prediction <- ru_apply("predict_regression", d, x="speed", y="dist",
                       new_x=15.5, confidence=.95)
stopifnot(nrow(prediction)==1L,all(is.finite(prediction)))
```

The interval describes uncertainty about a new stopping-distance observation at the chosen speed under the model, not merely the uncertainty in the fitted mean. It does not justify predictions beyond observed speeds.

## Apply to another dataset

```r
ru_apply("predict_regression", your_data, x="predictor", y="outcome", new_x=15.5, confidence=.95)
```

A confidence interval for the mean fitted response is narrower than an interval for a future individual observation.

Review assumptions and available input conditions with `ru_plan("predict_regression")`. A valid computation does not itself verify the underlying study design.
